Anathema

uh-NATH-uh-muh · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anathema is a thing or person that is intensely disliked or detested.

Silence during a movie was anathema to her -- she couldn't sit through a single scene without whispering commentary.

Worked Example

To the minimalist architect, ornate decoration of any kind was anathema; even a single decorative molding was enough to make him walk out of a project.

Anathema names a thing that is intensely disliked or detested -- the architect doesn't just dislike ornate decoration, he treats it as something to be avoided entirely.

How Anathema Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

abomination

abomination: a thing that causes disgust or hatred

bane

bane: a cause of great distress or annoyance

Antonyms

delight

delight: great pleasure

favorite

favorite: a person or thing especially liked

How Strong Is It? — dislike → anathema → loathing

dislike vs. anathema

dislike vs. anathema: Dislike is a general negative preference, without the intensity of something treated as forbidden.

loathing vs. anathema

loathing vs. anathema: Loathing is an intense, personal disgust -- an even stronger feeling than treating something as anathema.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ana-

prefix — ana-: up, back, again (Greek)

root — thema

root — thema: something placed or set down; a thing set apart (Greek tithenai, 'to place')

Put it together

Put it together: Anathema comes from Greek ana- ('back, apart') + tithenai ('to place') -- originally 'a thing set apart' (as a curse), which came to mean something intensely disliked.

Root Check

Word Choice

Anathema names the object of intense dislike -- 'X is anathema to Y' -- which makes it grammatically different from abhorrent (an adjective describing a thing's own repulsive quality) and from misanthrope (a person who dislikes people in general, not one specific thing).
